extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and third-party requesters handling ex parte reexamination requests under 35 U.S.C. 302
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what prior art (patents and printed publications) may be considered when determining whether a 'substantial new question of patentability' exists in requests filed under 35 U.S.C. 302. Covers sources of prior art, when examiners may search for additional art, and which claims are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination may be based on any prior art patents or printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination under 35 U.S.C. 303(a) whether or not 'a substantial new question of patentability' is present can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not limited to the patents and printed publications relied on in the request; the examiner can find a substantial new question of patentability based upon (a) the prior art relied on in the request, (b) a combination of the prior art relied on in the request and other prior art found elsewhere, or (c) entirely different patents or printed publications. The primary source, however, are the patents and printed publications relied on in the request. (See also reference to MPEP §2242 for 'old art' discussion for reexaminations ordered on/after Nov. 2, 2002.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority to consider other patents/printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 303(a) and 37 CFR 1.515(a) provide that the determination on a request will be made 'with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications,' i.e., other than those relied upon in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory/regulatory language authorizes the examiner to consider other prior art beyond what the requester cited when deciding whether a substantial new question of patentability exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of patents/printed publications of record from 37 CFR 1.501 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner can also consider any patents and printed publications of record in the patent file from submissions under 37 CFR 1.501 which are in compliance with 37 CFR 1.98 in making the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions to the patent file that comply with 37 CFR 1.98 and are entered under 37 CFR 1.501 may serve as prior art of record for purposes of deciding whether a substantial new question exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority to perform additional targeted searches to supply prior art deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that additional prior art patents and publications can be readily obtained by searching to supply any deficiencies in the prior art cited in the request, the examiner can perform such an additional search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any additional search should be limited to the area most likely to contain the deficiency of the prior art previously considered, and should be made only where there is a reasonable likelihood that prior art can be found to supply any deficiency necessary to 'a substantial new question of patentability.' The search must therefore be targeted and justified by a reasonable likelihood of finding relevant art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered for determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination should be made on the claims in effect at the time the decision is made (37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of whether a substantial new question of patentability exists must reference the claim set currently in force when the examiner makes the decision; amended/changed claims at the time of decision govern the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority and purpose of the 'substantial new question' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has the authority to order reexamination only in those cases which raise a substantial new question of patentability. The substantial new question of patentability requirement protects patentees from having to respond to, or participate in unjustified reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a threshold protection for patentees; the Director should order reexamination only where the statutory/regulatory standard of a substantial new question is met. (See cited case Patlex Corp. v. Mossinghoff, 771 F.2d 480, 226 USPQ 985 (Fed. Cir. 1985).)
